subject: maths
title: Midpoints, lengths and shapes on the Cartesian plane

lines.say: These two points have the same y. So the segment is flat.
Its length is the difference of the x values.
It crosses the y-axis, so you go through zero. Not 5 take 4.
Same x means vertical. Subtract the y values instead.
The midpoint is exactly halfway along a segment.
Average the x values. Minus 4 plus 6 is 2. Halve it: 1.
Average the y values. 3 plus minus 5 is minus 2. Halve it: minus 1.
So the midpoint M is 1, minus 1.
Check. A to M is 5 right, 4 down. M to B is the same.
Midpoint equals mean point. Add, then divide by 2.
M is 2, minus 1. It's the midpoint of A, minus 3, 4, and B. Find B.
The step from A to M is 5 right and 5 down.
Do the same step again from M. That lands on 7, minus 6.
Don't average A and M. That gives a point between them.
Triangle P, Q, R. P and Q both have y equal to minus 2.
lines.alt: Triangle PQR with a dashed height from R to PQ

lines.say: So PQ is the base. 5 take minus 3 is 8 units.
The height is from R down to the base. 4 take minus 2 is 6.
Half of base times height. 8 times 6, halved, is 24.
The height is a distance from the base, not a y value.

frames.heading: Box it and chop the corners

lines.say: This triangle has no flat or upright side. Draw a box round it.
The box is 6 by 6. That's 36 square units.
Cut off the three corner triangles: 6, 9 and 6.
What's left is the triangle. 36 take 21 is 15.
Don't forget to halve. The midpoint is not just the sum.
Mind the signs. From minus 4 to 5 is 9, not 1.
Triangles and trapeziums both need dividing by 2.
Sketch first. You'll see which sides are flat.
Same y: horizontal. Same x: vertical. Subtract the ones that change.
Midpoint is the mean of the x's and the mean of the y's.
Missing endpoint? Same step again.
Slanted shape? Box it, then chop off the corners.
